Trip journal

The real version of the itinerary: detours, favorite views, tour-guide facts, and the little moments worth keeping.

Day One · Saturday, September 12

The road made the day

Complete

We left right on time around 9:00 AM, aiming for Trail of the Cedars and maybe Avalanche Lake. After thirty minutes of hunting for parking without luck, we let the plan go and followed Going-to-the-Sun Road instead.

The change of plans became the day: pull-off after pull-off, photos everywhere, the Weeping Wall, Bird Woman Falls, and one enormous mountain overlook that became our favorite stop and delivered some of our best pictures. We made it to Logan Pass, used the area to turn around, and saved the hiking for another time.

Back at Lake McDonald Lodge, we had lunch and wandered the lakefront before taking a quick car nap ahead of our 5:30 PM boat cruise. The hour on Lake McDonald came with stories about the 2018 fire, fire-resistant trees, the rainforest-like west side of the lake, and a ghostly submerged forest said to sit about 80 feet below the surface for scuba divers to see.

We also heard the road's movie connections and managed to stump our guide by asking how many trees are in Glacier National Park. No one had the answer. After the cruise, we stocked up on groceries for the week and called it a night completely exhausted.

Favorite moment

That giant mountain overlook on Going-to-the-Sun Road — the view, the photos, and the feeling that the unexpected route was exactly the right one.

A planned hike became a scenic-road day · Lake McDonald boat cruise at 5:30 PM
Day Two · Sunday, September 13

Rainy-day detours

In progress

Rain called for a softer start: extra sleep, a slow morning, and a shift away from the original plan. We went to Whitefish Lake State Park for a look at the water, then drove through downtown Whitefish without stopping in the rain.

Next came West Glacier Village for souvenir browsing and a photo with the Glacier sign at the shops — not the national-park sign. Then we headed for Hungry Horse Dam, briefly taking the wrong address and arriving at the bottom in a service area before figuring it out and making our way back to the top.

We returned to basecamp for burgers and an easy hangout while the day was still unfolding.

Plot twist

Accidentally finding the bottom of Hungry Horse Dam first, then navigating our way back up to the overlook.

Open decisions

Two calls still to make, each with a hard "decide by" so a booking window doesn't close.

Flag 1

Grinnell Lake — boat or on foot?

by Mon 9/14 PM

The boat-assisted version crosses Swiftcurrent + Josephine, then has a 1.8 mi round trip walk to Grinnell Lake. It includes a 0.2 mi, 80 ft steep connector between the two boat docks, so it is not entirely flat. Tours can sell out — if you want this version, book it now. $41.70 pp.

The on-foot version is flat lakeshore, ~6.8 mi round trip, no advance booking — that call can wait until Tuesday morning at the trailhead.

Flag 2

Grinnell Glacier — only if the knee is holding up

choose before booking a boat

Go only if the knee handled Saturday and Sunday with no next-day trouble — and you're both up for a 5–6 hr trail day.

Realistic form: an 11 AM boat still means leaving basecamp about 7:15 AM to arrive an hour early. Full hike with the boat is 7.6 mi RT / 1,600 ft and can run into the final 5:45 PM return boat. Treat it as a full-day choice, not an add-on to the baseline.

  • Lake Josephine — ~2 mi in, flat. Turn here and it's basically the baseline day.
  • Base of the switchbacks — ~3.3 mi, before the real climb. Good "we got the views" stop.
  • Anywhere on the ascent — the payoff builds gradually; even halfway is spectacular.

Packing — carry-on only

One roller + one daypack each (the daypack is your plane personal item and your trail bag). Tap to check off, add your own, delete what you overrule. Saved on this device.

Won't fly — plan around it

  • Bear spray — prohibited in carry-on and checked. Buy it in Montana (~$50), leave or gift it at the end.
  • Trekking poles — not allowed in carry-on. Buy a cheap pair in Kalispell/Whitefish or rent in Apgar — worth it for the knee on any downhill.
  • Liquids — 3-1-1: nothing over 3.4 oz, one quart bag each. Sunscreen and bug spray in travel sizes.
  • No checked bag for 7 days — pack for ~4 days + one mid-trip laundry (detergent sheets), or 7 of the small stuff.
0 packed

Plan around

Alpine weather, a fire-season wildcard, and a rental we'd like to return unscratched.

Wildfire smoke protocol

  • Check each morning — AirNow + the NPS conditions page before committing the day
  • West socked in? The east side (St. Mary, Many Glacier) often clears on an east wind — and vice versa
  • Swap freely: Wed and Thu are flexible; Sun (GTSR) and Tue (Many Glacier) are the anchors — move them relative to each other
  • Snow: a September storm can shut Logan Pass for a day — flip to a valley or Whitefish day if so

Driving notes

  • No fuel inside the park — top off in Columbia Falls or St. Mary before park days
  • Going-to-the-Sun Road — narrow, cliff-edge, ~40 mph max; the drive itself takes ~2 hrs one way
  • No cell service on GTSR, Many Glacier, or the North Fork — download offline maps first
  • Logan Pass parking — the 2026 timed-parking pilot ended Sept 7; parking is still first-come, so aim to arrive by ~10 AM
  • Skip the dirt — Bowman Lake Rd and the far North Fork are washboard; not for the sedan

Field notes

Why the water is that color

Glacial meltwater carries "rock flour" — silt ground fine by moving ice. It scatters light toward that milky turquoise, strongest in bright afternoon sun.

The Divide splits the weather

The Continental Divide runs down the park's spine. West and east can differ by 15°F and a whole sky. Pack for both, every day.

Larches turn late September

Alpine larch — the conifer that drops its needles — goes gold in the high basins right around your dates. Watch for the first of it near Logan Pass.

No reservations in 2026

The timed-entry system is suspended park-wide this year. Just drive in with a pass. The only pinch is Logan Pass parking.

Not a backup this week

Two Medicine is closed beyond Running Eagle Falls from Sept 8 for utility and road work. Keep Wednesday and Thursday as the flexible swaps instead.
